name: Nickel monoxide
description: Nickel monoxide (CAS 1313-99-1 ), commercially known as black nickel oxide, is an inorganic compound used primarily as a colorant, surface modifier, and reactive component across industrial manufacturing. It delivers controlled coloration and chemical reactivity in high-temperature and specialty coating processes. In coatings and surface treatments, it acts as a pigment and adhesion promoter. This compound contributes to durable, corrosion-resistant finishes on metal substrates. Printing ink formulators incorporate it to achieve stable, heat-resistant black tones in specialty packaging inks. These inks are designed for demanding print environments where stability is key. Elastomer and sealant manufacturers use it as a curing co-agent and surface modifier to improve bonding performance. It enhances the connection between rubber compounds and metal components. In personal care, it appears in select cosmetic formulations as a colorant where regulatory compliance is a critical consideration. Particle consistency remains a vital sourcing factor for these applications. The product is supplied as a fine black powder in technical and industrial grades for various manufacturing needs. Particle size distribution and purity levels are key specification parameters buyers should confirm with suppliers. These factors directly affect pigment performance and reactivity in formulation. Standard packaging ranges from multi-wall bags to bulk containers depending on order volume. Ensuring the correct grade is essential for maintaining quality standards across all industrial sectors.
